subject: Intro: Candidate Alex Tang — Backend ML Infra
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah@latticebridge.com>

Subject: Intro: Alex Tang — Backend ML infra candidate

Hi Vivek — quick intro from LatticeBridge.

Alex Tang is a senior backend engineer with strong ML infra experience (builds inference pipelines, caching, autoscaling hooks). They are actively interviewing and asked us to prioritize roles at companies with production inference challenges — sounded like Redwood is a good match after our call.

I attached Alex's resume and a short intake summary. Can you confirm whether the team has 45–60 minute panel availability on Tue/Wed next week? Alex prefers mornings PST but can shift.

Proposed panel: Eng manager + 1 infra engineer + 1 product/PM. We can run a live system design + 20m Q&A.

Candidate: Alex Tang
Location: SF Bay Area (remote ok)
Notice: 2 weeks
Comp expectations: open to discussion

Attachments: alex_tang_resume.pdf, latticebridge_intake_summary.pdf

Thanks — happy to coordinate slots or send a Calendly link.

—Sarah Lim
Senior Recruiter | LatticeBridge
sarah@latticebridge.com
(415) 555-0123

Thanks Sarah — appreciate the intro and the intake doc.

Marissa/Laura — looped you in for scheduling and a quick read. Our preference for this role is a short take-home + 45m panel, but given Alex is senior we can do a live system-design first and skip the take-home if the panel agrees.

Marissa, do you want to lead the tech panel? If so, can you propose 3 morning windows (PST) Tue/Wed next week that work for you + one infra engineer? I can cover PM alignment.

Sarah — if you can share Alex's Calendly or available windows we can match. If you prefer, I can send a Doodle or propose direct times.

Forwarding Alex's resume here for quick reference.

Subject: Re: Intro: Alex Tang — Backend ML infra (availability)

Thanks, Sarah.

I can run the tech panel. Proposed windows (all PST, 45m):
- Tue 2026-11-09 09:00–09:45
- Tue 2026-11-09 10:30–11:15
- Wed 2026-11-10 09:30–10:15

Laura — can you and one infra engineer join any of those? If not, tell me two slots that work for you and I will coordinate.

If Alex prefers mornings, the Tue 9:00 slot is ideal. Sarah, can you confirm Alex's availability for those slots? We'll keep the agenda: 20–25m system design (inference pipelines, scaling), 15–20m technical Q&A, 5–10m culture/PM questions.

Also: if Alex is flexible we can do a 60m panel at 10:30 so folks have some buffer.

—Marissa Cole

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-03T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Alex Tang — Backend ML infra (post-interview notes)

On Tue, Nov 2, 2026 at 09:12, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Sarah.
>
> I can run the tech panel. Proposed windows (all PST, 45m):
> - Tue 2026-11-09 09:00–09:45
> - Tue 2026-11-09 10:30–11:15
> - Wed 2026-11-10 09:30–10:15

Follow-up — we ran the panel this morning (Alex joined at 09:05). Quick notes:
- Technical depth: strong practical experience with building KV cache layers and async batchers; answered scaling questions with concrete tradeoffs.
- Systems design: proposed a reasonable approach for prefix caching + TTL invalidation; flagged a couple edge cases around multi-tenant cache poisoning that I pushed on.
- Communication: clear, concise, asked good clarifying questions.

Red flags: none obvious. Candidate had limited hands-on work with HSM/KMS integrations (we asked); seems comfortable learning.

Recommend: move to final on-site loop with infra engineer and PM (60m). Preferred hire level: Senior Engineer.

Sarah — can you hold Alex for a final loop and check compensation expectations in writing? If all good, we can send an internal calendar invite and a short mutual action plan.

Attachments: short panel rubric (attached internally)

—Laura Bennett
Senior Staff Engineer | Redwood Inference
